headline: High-risk default egress and shared-MCP interaction create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; B is locally constrained but A is not.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use MCP, browsers, and broad network egress, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content and pass it onward. Agent B has no documented input isolation or provenance checks, but its network_egress is none, so the main risk is A-to-B content poisoning rather than remote exfiltration. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests web or file content and forwards it to agent_b without provenance labels
IF agent_b treats agent_a output as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding from A to B
Require explicit provenance tags on A outputs
Strip instructions from imported text before B reads it
Use a manual review step for any A-generated content
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and has broad egress plus API-key handling, while agent B has no documented data classes and no network egress. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is not established; however, if files are shared, A could transmit sensitive document contents externally. B itself is locally constrained, reducing blast radius.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or workspace
IF sensitive PDFs or text files are opened by A and then copied into B
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in files processed by A
Turn off A network egress when handling sensitive documents
Review any exported artifacts before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while B has no documented write or network capabilities. There is no evidence of overlapping write surfaces, shared mutable resources, or locking conflicts. The pairwise conflict pathway is therefore limited and mostly hypothetical unless an external orchestrator gives both agents the same writable target.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF both agents are allowed to modify the same file or repository
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent edits to shared artifacts
Use file locks for any shared target
requires-engineering: add conflict detection on shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and B is a travel-planning sample with no documented verification layer. If B consumes A's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into downstream actions or plans. B's lack of network egress limits harm, but the default trust pathway remains plausible and unmitigated.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks A's claims before B acts
mitigations: Add a verification step before B consumes A output
Require citations for any factual claims from A
Flag low-confidence A outputs for review
Keep B in read-only mode for A-derived content
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles API keys and broad egress, which can create retention or residency concerns if regulated documents are processed, while B has no documented sensitive-data handling or egress. No specific residency mismatch or regulated data class is documented for B, so compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch if sensitive inputs are introduced into A.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed by agent_a
IF organizational policy forbids external API transmission of those documents
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to A
Review vendor retention settings before use
Use redacted inputs for A
Document data-handling policy for the pair
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
